Title: Diagnosis of test `testGenerateURLFragment`
Details: The test `testGenerateURLFragment` checks whether HTML entities such as `"` are correctly escaped to their corresponding character by the `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` method. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case. Following the execution path, we find that `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` is not escaping any HTML code; instead, it is using its input `toolTipText` as is. Consequently, un-escaped strings are being returned, which leads to the error demonstrated by the test.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis of test `testFinish`

Details: The failing test `testFinish` in `ArchiveOutputStreamTest` verifies behavior of the `finish()` method for various archive output streams after putting an archive entry but before closing the entry. The test expects an IOException to be thrown if `finish()` is called immediately after `putArchiveEntry()` without calling `closeArchiveEntry()` (or similar).

The failure is specifically with the "tar" archive type: the call to `finish()` on the `TarArchiveOutputStream` instance does not throw the expected IOException, causing the test assertion to fail and signal "After putArchive should follow closeArchive".

The test tries this sequence for "zip", "jar", "ar", "cpio" and "tar" archive output streams. For all but `tar`, the test passes (meaning they correctly throw the IOException), but for `tar`, no exception is thrown.

This indicates there is a discrepancy in the implementation of `TarArchiveOutputStream.finish()` or related state checks versus other archive types' finish implementations. There might be a missing guard to ensure `finish()` cannot be called before closing the current archive entry.

Next, investigate the code of `TarArchiveOutputStream.finish()` to verify if it checks for a currently open entry before finishing and throws IOException if so. This will help confirm why no exception is thrown for tar.

I will now retrieve the code snippet for `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveOutputStream.finish()`.
